items.reason: Describes the missing GRANT_TYPE assignment in client-credentials issuance, which causes the encoder to use the unknown 'na' shortcut.
Describes the incorrect grant substring offset and inverted equality check in isAccessTokenId.
Describes the same matcher offset and comparison errors that allow incorrect grant shortcuts to pass.
Describes the documentation recommending three-letter shortcuts despite the encoding requiring exactly two characters.
Describes the duplicated grantType null check that leaves rawTokenId unvalidated and allows ':null' encoding.
Describes the incorrect grant offset and inverted comparison that prevent event assertions from verifying the grant.
Describes the same isAccessTokenId substring and equality errors that accept tokens from the wrong grant.
Describes the three-letter shortcut contract conflicting with the two-character encoding requirement, including the missing width validation already reported under this issue.
Describes checking grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null to serialize as 'null'.
Describes missing shortcut-width validation and the misleading three-letter documentation, both covered by this issue's existing reports.
Describes lazy registration overwriting shortcut ownership without uniqueness checks, causing existing tokens to decode as another grant.
Describes the incorrect substring offset and inverted equality check that let incorrect grant prefixes pass the matcher.
Describes the repeated grantType validation leaving rawTokenId unchecked and allowing null IDs to be encoded.
